§2.3 Traceability

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

principles-traceability · principles boxes

✅ Normative

Every element of the output MUST be attributable to the place on the page it was read from. When boxes are requested, every Markdown element MUST have a box, and every box MUST cover exactly the printed content of its element.

Traceability is what lets a reader of the Markdown — a person or a model — go back to the page to check, cite or highlight a statement. It is also what makes the two principles checkable: a Markdown element with no printed source is invented; printed content with no Markdown element is dropped.

  • An element is traced by its box: the region of the page its content occupies. What a box covers and how fine boxes go are defined in Boxes and Granularity§3.3; how boxes are carried is defined in The Sidecar§3.4.
  • Content the protocol moves out of its printed position — a watermark placed first, a sidenote placed after its paragraph, a folio recorded on its own — still traces to where it was printed.
  • A Markdown element that was synthesised rather than transcribed (for example a chart table built from marks) traces to the region of the page it was read from.
